answer: In an agent economy, new identities gain standing only after an established peer issues a unique marble seal that binds a personal jade compute token—derived from a sequential lantern challenge using the peer's latest attested history—to the applicant's key. Each peer has a hard cap of three seals per epoch and risks locked stake if the recipient later fails graded work. Scaling a farm forces the attacker to recruit or bribe many independent peers whose lantern slots cannot be parallelized or reused, so the marginal cost of each extra fake rises as available honest sponsors dwindle.
